name: Torque
simple: Torque is an invisible twister. It keeps twisting a part with the same strength all the time, so the part spins faster and faster. You choose which way it twists with a Vector3: the direction of the vector is the line it spins around.
analogy: Torque is like a friend who keeps flicking a fidget spinner. Every flick adds more spin, so it goes faster and faster unless something slows it down.
whenToUse: Make an object spin up over time
Wheels or propellers that you want to speed up gradually
Twisting an object over when hit
where: Create with Instance.new("Torque") and set Attachment0 to an attachment in the part to spin. It always twists around the part's center of mass. Usually set up from a Script on the server.

terms.torque: A twisting push that makes things spin, like turning a doorknob or a steering wheel. Torque = force x distance from the spinning point, so pushing farther from the center twists harder.
terms.angular velocity: How fast something spins, and around which axis, measured in radians per second. 2 x pi (about 6.28) radians per second is one full turn every second.
terms.radians: Another way to measure angles. A full circle is 2 x pi (about 6.28) radians, which is 360 degrees. `math.rad(90)` turns 90 degrees into radians.
terms.Vector3: Three numbers (X, Y, Z) bundled together. Used for positions, directions, forces and speeds. Y is up.
terms.attachment: A tiny invisible point you put inside a part. It has a position AND a direction (its own X, Y and Z arrows). Constraints grab parts by their attachments.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachments a constraint connects. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed or moved; Attachment1 is the other end or the goal.
terms.assembly: A group of parts that are rigidly joined (for example by welds) so they move as one solid object. A force on any part moves the whole group.
terms.unanchored: A part that physics is allowed to move. Constraints that push or pull only work on unanchored parts.
terms.center of mass: The balance point of an object. Pushing exactly through it moves the object without spinning it; pushing off to the side also makes it spin.
terms.world space: Directions measured using the whole game world's fixed arrows: Y is always straight up toward the sky, no matter how a part is turned.
terms.attachment space: Directions measured using an attachment's own arrows. If the part tips over, 'up' for the attachment tips over too.
terms.RelativeTo: Chooses whose arrows the numbers use: World (the game world's fixed directions) or Attachment0/Attachment1 (that attachment's own directions, which turn when the part turns).
terms.spin axis: The imaginary stick something spins around. A Torque of Vector3.new(0, 500, 0) spins around the up-down (Y) line, like a merry-go-round.
terms.constant torque: A twist that never changes strength, so the spin speed keeps growing until friction or something else stops it.

examples.title: Spin a floating part like a top
examples.code:
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Size = Vector3.new(4, 1, 2)
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
part.Anchored = false
part.Parent = workspace

local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
attachment.Parent = part

-- Hold it up so it does not fall (see VectorForce)
local hover = Instance.new("VectorForce")
hover.Attachment0 = attachment
hover.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
hover.ApplyAtCenterOfMass = true
hover.Force = Vector3.new(0, part.AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity, 0)
hover.Parent = part

-- Twist it around the up (Y) axis
local twist = Instance.new("Torque")
twist.Attachment0 = attachment
twist.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
twist.Torque = Vector3.new(0, 50, 0)
twist.Parent = part

task.wait(2)
twist.Enabled = false -- stop adding spin; it keeps spinning at its current speed
print("Spin speed:", part.AssemblyAngularVelocity.Y, "radians per second")
explain: First we cancel gravity with a VectorForce so the part floats.
Torque (0, 50, 0) in World space means 'twist around the up-down line'.
Each moment, the twist adds more spin, so after 2 seconds it is spinning much faster than after 1.
When we turn the Torque off, nothing slows the floating part, so it keeps the spin it already has.

gotchas: Torque never stops adding spin, so things can end up spinning extremely fast. Use AngularVelocity if you want a steady spin speed.
A part sitting on the ground has friction holding it. Small torques may do nothing; try bigger numbers.
Big or heavy parts need much more torque to spin than small light ones.
With RelativeTo = Attachment0 (the default), the spin axis turns with the part. Use World if you want it to always spin around the true up direction.

Torque.RelativeTo.simple: Picks whose directions the Torque vector uses: World (the game's fixed directions), Attachment0 (default; turns with the part), or Attachment1 (follows the other attachment).
Torque.RelativeTo.example:
local twist = workspace.Top.Torque
twist.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World -- always spin around the real up axis

Torque.Torque.simple: How hard and around which line to twist, as a Vector3. (0, 50, 0) twists around Y; (50, 0, 0) around X. A negative number twists the other way.
Torque.Torque.example:
local twist = workspace.Top.Torque
twist.Torque = Vector3.new(0, -50, 0) -- spin the opposite direction
